clue.text: Book for Sunday opening — put in the one before Easter

indicators.note: put in tells us one piece is placed inside the other here

parts.note: Palm Sunday is the Sunday before Easter, so the one before Easter is Palms

indicators.note: opening asks for just the first letter of the word Sunday

explanation.surface: A churchgoer chooses a reading for the start of the Sunday before Easter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sunday' is not part of the Palm Sunday phrase in the wordplay: its first letter S is what goes inside PALMS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Psalms form a book of the Old Testament, so a book of scripture fits.

clue.text: Father not quite head?

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls a little short, losing its final letter

parts.note: pater is Latin, and old schoolboy slang, for father

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a dad is almost the boss of the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Pate is an old or humorous word for the top of the skull, the crown of one's head.

clue.text: Explorer's friend embracing monarch

definitions.note: read as Explorer is, the 's standing for is

indicators.note: embracing means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: amigo is Spanish for friend, familiar in English
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword monarch

explanation.surface: A traveller's companion hugs the king or queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Explorer's is read as 'Explorer is', not as a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Amerigo Vespucci was the Italian navigator after whom America is named, a famous explorer.

clue.text: 21, perhaps, top line in Bond's "Who's Who"?

definitions.meaning: in the James Bond stories M heads the secret service

explanation.surface: A James Bond cast list opens with a teasing hint of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into M IS CHIEF: M is the head of MI6 in the Bond books.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkey business is playful naughtiness, which is mischief, and the split phrase describes Bond's spymaster boss.

clue.text: Beast interchanged in opening

parts.note: an ape is a beast
read as inter-changed: the letters of inter rearranged give RIENT

explanation.surface: An animal is swapped around inside a gap.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is to split 'interchanged' into 'inter' plus 'changed': changed is the anagram signal for those five letters. 'in' is part of that split word, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperient is a mild laxative, a medicine that opens the bowels, so it is an opening medicine.

clue.text: Our second XI (beginners) in colour, Saints having no goals

indicators.note: in tells us the first letters are placed inside the colour

parts.note: purple is a colour

indicators.note: beginners asks for the first letter of each of the words that come before it

parts.note: XI is the Roman numeral for eleven, so its beginning is E

explanation.surface: A club's reserve team, kitted out in their colours, faces a Saints side that cannot score.
explanation.walkthrough: XI must first be read as ELEVEN before its first letter is taken, so the beginners are O, S and E, which sit inside PURPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Purposeless means without aim, and goals here are aims rather than football scores.

clue.text: Pieces of furniture now named "Glory"

indicators.note: pieces of means the letters run across parts of the following words

explanation.surface: A furniture range is now marketed under the brand name Glory.
explanation.definitionFit: Renown is fame or great honour, the same as glory.

clue.text: Book with 1 across and sleep it off

indicators.note: off suggests something gone bad or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone reads the Psalms and then sleeps off a heavy night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book with 1 across' means a book of the Bible alongside the Psalms. 'off' signals an anagram of SLEEP IT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Epistles are letters forming books of the New Testament, so one is a Bible book like the Psalms.

clue.text: Mixed grill — yet I will have it in bed

indicators.note: mixed means the letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone refuses a mixed grill but would happily eat it in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' looks like a bedroom, but it is a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger lily is a garden flower that grows in a flower bed.

clue.text: Believer has time for crime

parts.note: a heist is a robbery, a crime

explanation.surface: A man of faith has done time for an offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word, not an exchange: T simply sits before HEIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A theist believes in God or gods, so a theist is a believer.

clue.text: Lodger keeps Alsatian largely to make an impression

indicators.note: keeps means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: PG, a paying guest, is a lodger

indicators.note: largely means most of the word is used, with its last part dropped

parts.note: Rin Tin Tin was the famous German shepherd (Alsatian) film dog

explanation.surface: A lodger keeps a big German shepherd in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: Alsatian is the British name for a German shepherd; Rin Tin Tin was the canine star of Hollywood films, and 'largely' drops his final TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Printing makes impressions of type on paper, so it is the act of impressing.

clue.text: Stranded creature to save from drowning?

definitions.meaning: an animal left on dry land, or in idiom a person out of place
literally, pulling a swimmer from the water to land them on dry land

explanation.surface: A rescuer pulls a stranded animal from the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a creature or person out of its element, and literally means pulling something from water.

clue.text: Loveless marriage and being dressed like a nun is desert

parts.note: marriage is a union; loveless takes away the O, love being zero in tennis
habited means wearing a habit, the robe of a nun

explanation.surface: A loveless marriage and a life in a nun's habit are a wilderness.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O, as a zero score in tennis, so the loveless union is UNIN. 'desert' is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert island is an uninhabited one, so desert as an adjective means empty of people.

clue.text: Source of 1 down, sticky stuff, with return of abuses

parts.note: goo is sticky stuff

indicators.note: return of means the following word is read backwards

parts.note: to revile is to abuse in words

explanation.surface: A recipe uses something sticky while someone hurls insults back.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 down is PATE, the head, but here its other sense of pâté is meant; REVILES backwards gives SELIVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Foie gras pâté is made from goose liver, so it is the source of that pâté.

clue.text: Ancient compiler died in embrace of girl — first prize!

indicators.note: in embrace of means the pieces are held inside the next one

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
ancient means old
the compiler is the setter, who refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: An elderly puzzle setter dies in a girl's arms and is rewarded.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often call themselves 'the compiler' or 'this setter', so the word stands for ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold medal is awarded for first place in a competition, the top prize.

clue.text: Risk foreign article being closest to satellite

parts.note: peril is risk or danger
une is the French indefinite article

explanation.surface: A dangerous foreign article reports on getting nearest to a satellite.
explanation.definitionFit: Perilune is the point in a lunar orbit closest to the moon, a natural satellite.

clue.text: Amazingly, a lost Daniel's holding on here

indicators.note: holding means the shortened name contains the next piece
amazingly suggests something unexpected, so the letters are shuffled
lost means the preceding letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Somehow the biblical Daniel, though lost, is still holding on.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the A from DANIELS to get DNIELS, put ON in it, and 'Amazingly' rearranges the lot; Daniel was thrown into the lions' den in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible places Daniel in the lions' den, the place meant by here.

clue.text: See 14
Figure of horse in 12

indicators.note: in means the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: twelve o'clock midday is noon
a nag is a horse

explanation.surface: A cross-reference asks for the shape of a horse in the twelfth clue.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' looks like a cross-reference to 12 down, but it is just the number twelve: noon.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonagon is a geometrical figure with nine sides.

clue.text: Woman begins episcopate, nothing less than perfect, as if unsure of her welcome

definitions.text: as if unsure of her welcome

parts.note: she refers to a woman

indicators.note: begins means only the opening of the word episcopate is kept, its tail dropped
less than means the first word is taken away from the second

parts.note: holy means perfect in goodness
O, like zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A woman becomes a bishop, but not quite perfectly, and seems unsure of her reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'begins' keeps just the start of episcopate, EPIS; O is taken from HOLY to give HLY. The surface plays on the debate over women bishops.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting sheepishly is acting embarrassed or diffident, as one unsure of being welcome would.

clue.text: Film hid in stockings for refuge

indicators.note: hid in means the first piece is tucked inside the other

parts.note: hose are stockings
pic is short for picture, a film

explanation.surface: A film reel was hidden in stockings to keep it safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospice was originally a shelter for travellers, so it is a refuge.

clue.text: Kickback for providing fuel for play area

parts.note: rec, short for recreation ground, is a play area
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: A bribe is paid for supplying fuel to a playground.
explanation.walkthrough: A rec, a recreation ground, is a British public park or playing field. 'Kickback' looks like a bribe, but it is a gun's recoil.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun's kickback is its recoil, the jolt backwards on firing.

clue.text: Monarch in finance matters means hanky-panky

indicators.note: in means the monarch goes inside the next piece

parts.note: finance means money
K is the abbreviation for king, a monarch
business means matters or affairs

explanation.surface: A ruler involved in money matters is guilty of misconduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkey business is mischievous or dishonest behaviour, which is hanky-panky.

clue.text: Poker in the nose or ear?

definitions.meaning: a variety of the card game in which some cards are dealt face up
a small piece of jewellery pushed through a pierced nose or ear

explanation.surface: Someone asks where a poker might be poked, nose or ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Stud is a form of poker and also a piercing ornament worn in a nose or ear.

clue.text: Norman architectural feature, the same to put in much of Gothic

parts.note: do, short for ditto, means the same

indicators.note: put in means one piece is inserted into the other
much of means the word loses its final part

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A design detail of Norman buildings resembles Gothic work.
explanation.walkthrough: DO is the conventional short form of ditto, used in lists to mean the same again.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogtooth is a carved ornament of pointed, tooth-like shapes found in Norman and early Gothic architecture.

clue.text: Publicity for split has gone wrong

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is publicity
a rift is a split

explanation.surface: An advertising campaign for a separation has backfired.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans that are adrift have gone awry, off course, so the word describes something that has gone wrong.

clue.text: Boy goes round New York after boy with hostess

indicators.note: after means the next letter follows the boy
goes round means the first piece surrounds the next

parts.note: a lad is a boy
a lad is a boy
Y is the abbreviation for York

explanation.surface: A lad tours New York, then another, and both stay with a hostess.
explanation.walkthrough: New York is split: N goes inside the first LAD, giving LAND, and Y (York) follows the second LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlady is a woman who keeps lodgers or an inn, so she is a hostess to her guests.

clue.text: Truthfully could be denied?

indicators.note: could be means these letters may become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a statement could truly be denied.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed means in truth or really, so it means truthfully.
